name: Chilean Skua
rangeDescription: Coasts of southern chile and southern argentina; ranges north to tropics
description: Rather large, dark, stocky gull-like seabird with big white wing patches (seen in flight). In summer often seen flying over Patagonian steppe or associating with Kelp Gulls at beaches, dumps, river mouths, and lakes near the coast.

name: Jandaya Parakeet
rangeDescription: Lowlands of northeastern brazil (eastern pará and goiás to alagoas)
description: Strikingly colored parakeet with a yellow head and chest, orange around the eyes and bill, orange on the belly, and blue flight feathers. Highly gregarious and noisy; can be seen flying over forests, woodlands, and agricultural areas, as well as in cities.

name: Barred Hawk
rangeDescription: Montane forest of costa rica to colombia and northern ecuador
description: This montane raptor has very broad wings and a disproportionately short tail. The black hood is a good mark that stands out at a distance, but the namesake bars on the belly are thin and indistinct.

name: Salim Ali's Swift
rangeDescription: Eastern tibetan plateau, western sichuan; winter range unknown
description: A large scimitar-winged swift of valleys, cliffs, and gorges. Nests in buildings and rock crevices; often gives a chattering scream when entering and leaving the nest.

name: Papuan Frogmouth
rangeDescription: New guinea, including raja ampat islands (off western new guinea), aru islands (off southwestern new guinea), and northeastern australia (southward to townsville)
description: Very large nocturnal bird with

name: Rufous Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Alaska to northwestern usa; winters to southern mexico
description: Adult males are almost entirely orange with bright white chest and some green on the back (can be solid green like Allen's Hummingbird). Throat is iridescent, and depending on the light, can look anywhere from red to orange to yellow to lime green.

name: Graceful Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Southern new guinea, including aru islands (off southwestern new guinea), southern torres strait islands, and cape york peninsula
description: A small olive-gray honeyeater with a circular pale yellow cheek patch and a relatively fine bill. Can be confused with Lewin’s Honeyeater and Yellow-spotted Honeyeater, but note the shape of the cheek patch: crescent-shaped on Lewin’s Honeyeater and oval on Yellow-spotted Honeyeater.

name: Black-billed Gull
rangeDescription: South island (new zealand); winters to north island
description: Pale gull endemic to New Zealand. White with light gray wings and back.

name: White-browed Bushchat
rangeDescription: Arid plains of southern afghanistan, eastern pakistan, and northwestern india
description: A small stonechat-like bird with a relatively long, slim bill. Male has blackish upperparts, a dark face, a white chin, and a whitish, contrasting eyebrow.

name: Turkestan Ground-Jay
rangeDescription: Northern and central uzbekistan, southern kazakhstan, and northern and central turkmenistan; also isolated population in eastern kazakhstan (south of lake balkhash)
description: Odd dove-gray corvid with a slightly decurved bill. Note black lores, tail, and chest.

name: Eastern Wood-Pewee
rangeDescription: Breeds eastern north america; winters to northern bolivia and western brazil
description: Drab grayish-brown flycatcher found in forested areas and edges. Nondescript overall with two pale wingbars; bill usually shows extensive orange on lower mandible.

name: Parrot-billed Sparrow
rangeDescription: Far southeastern south sudan, southern ethiopia, eastern uganda, kenya, southern somalia, and northeastern tanzania
description: A drab sparrow of northeastern Africa. The head and underparts are gray, the wing and back are brown, and the rump is rufous.

name: Ayacucho Antpitta
rangeDescription: East slope of the andes of south-central peru (ayacucho, west of the río apurímac between the río mantaro and río pampas)
description: Medium-sized antpitta found only in a small area of the eastern Andes in south central Peru, not far from the city of the same name. Plumage is rich chestnut-brown with a hint of buff on the belly.

name: Altamira Yellowthroat
rangeDescription: Coastal northeastern mexico (southern tamaulipas, eastern san luis potosí, and northern veracruz)
description: Brightly plumaged yellowthroat, restricted to northeast Mexico. Favors reed beds and adjacent marshy vegetation around lakes and ponds, also locally in cane fields.

name: Cyprus Scops-Owl
rangeDescription: Cyprus
description: A small dark owl, intricately marked with black streaks and fine barring. Bright yellow eyes are set in a pale face ringed with black.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Sincora Antwren
rangeDescription: Serra do sincorá, in the chapada diamantina, bahia, brazil
description: Range-restricted antwren of the Serra do Sincorá. Males are brown above and black below, with a white eye-line that stretches down to the underparts.

name: Palawan Babbler
rangeDescription: Southwestern philippines (balabac and palawan)
description: A medium-sized bird of lowland forest tangles and bamboo on Palawan and Balabac. Medium-brown above with more rufous on the tail, shoulder, and forecrown.

name: Black Harrier
rangeDescription: Arid grassland of southern namibia, southwestern botswana, and south africa
description: A striking, mostly dark harrier with large white panels in the underwings, a white rump, and bands on the tail. The juvenile is brown with white flashes in the underwings and has a heavily-streaked chest.

name: Snares Snipe
rangeDescription: Snares islands (northeast, broughton, and alert stack)
description: A small, stocky wader endemic to New Zealand. Dark brown and black, with barred feathers on the belly.

name: Baird's Junco
rangeDescription: Mountains of southern baja california (sierra de la laguna)
description: Distinctive sparrow found only in Sierra de La Laguna mountains near the southern tip of the Baja Peninsula. Pale gray with rufous back usually extending onto wings, white outer tail feathers and a staring yellow eye.
